text:
liam: Heads up — saw a regression in TP all-reduce perf after the kernel-selector change yesterday. Small-frag throughput drops and tail latency spikes for seq lengths that produce ~512B-2KB messages.

anya: Which job/commit? can you paste the perf summary and the repro command?

liam: repro script I used: ```scripts/perf_tp_allreduce.sh --batch 8 --seq 32 --world-size 8 --iters 200``` ran on 8xA100. Before change ring and tree were auto-deciding; after change we always hit the same kernel and get bad latency. quick perf snippet: 
```
512B: ring bw 0.8GB/s, tree bw 1.6GB/s, p50 5.2ms -> 12.7ms
2KB: ring bw 4.2GB/s, tree bw 4.5GB/s, p50 2.1ms -> 2.5ms
8KB: ring bw 9.8GB/s, tree bw 9.1GB/s, p50 1.0ms -> 1.1ms
```

matt: interesting — looks like tree wins for the tiny messages. selector probably bumped the threshold that triggers tree fallback. The new kernel has an extra memcpy path for small fragments (to align to vector size) which kills latency.

sophia: also check KV cache behavior — we saw a change in caching that increases fragment churn, effectively increasing number of small allreduces per request. Could be orthogonal but amplifies the regression.

liam: good call, sophia. I traced traces and see many flushes at attention boundaries producing 3-4x more AllReduce calls per step.

anya: Can you try forcing algorithm to validate? e.g. `export NCCL_ALGO=tree` or `NCCL_ALGO=ring` + `export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` then rerun the script. If tree restores p50, that's confirmation.

liam: did that: with NCCL_ALGO=tree p50 for 512B goes back to ~4.9ms, throughput doubles. With ring it stays bad. NCCL logs show tree path selected but kernel selector still picking the old kernel on the compute side.

matt: so two levers: 1) kernel selector heuristic (size threshold) 2) batching/fusing of small KV-cache flushes. Short-term: lower the tree threshold to <4KB so NCCL uses tree more for these workloads. Mid-term: we should change kernel selector to avoid the extra memcpy for small-frag cases.

perf-bot: Perf dashboard updated: https://perf.redwood.internal/d/TP/allreduce-smallfrag?var-commit=abc1234 — regression +18% token cost on smallfrag benchmarks.

anya: Can we get a minimal patch to kernel selector to prefer tree for seq_len<=32 and add a toggle? also add a telemetry flag to count small allreduces per request so we can see KV cache impact.

liam: I'll open a PR with the selector tweak + test microbench. I'll also attach the microbench output in the PR. initial ticket: https://redwood/issue/INF-4123 created.

sophia: For longer term we should add a tuning job that runs microbench across msg sizes on each kernel change and fails CI if small-frag regressions >10% — caught this too late.

matt: agreed. For now, experiments to run (short checklist):
- force NCCL_ALGO=tree and rerun full workload (liam)
- run microbench across [256B,512B,1KB,2KB,4KB,8KB] and capture kernel choices (anya)
- count number of KV-cache flush-induced allreduces per request (sophia)
- prototype kernel change to remove memcpy for small-frag (matt)

liam: I'll post the microbench outputs in the PR. quick snippet of final run after forcing tree: ```512B p50 5.0ms bw 1.5GB/s``` so immediate improvement. Will coordinate on PR. :thumbsup:

anya: perfect. tagging infra on the ticket for CI perf job. thanks everyone. :rocket:
